name: Forge
text: We should focus on building packages first, as this will give us a solid foundation for the rest of our work. By doing so, we'll be able to create a consistent structure that will make it easier to enrich tabs and draft elements later on. This decision means we'll be delaying the enrichment of tabs and drafting of elements, but I believe it's a trade-off worth accepting because it will save us time and effort in the long run by reducing the need for rework and revisions. By prioritizing package building, we'll be putting quality first and setting ourselves up for success in achieving our goal.

name: Vet
text: Vet: Hold on—delaying tab enrichment isn’t just a delay, it’s a hidden bet that the package structure will *stay* solid enough to build on. What if the packages force us to redo tabs later because they’re too rigid? Instead, why not prototype one tab *while* building the first package? That way, we test both at once and spot mismatches early. Settle it by building a tiny tab mockup against the first package draft—if it breaks, we pivot; if it works, we scale.

name: Forge
text:
I think we should prototype one tab while building the first package, as Vet suggested. This approach allows us to test the package structure's flexibility and identify potential issues early on, which will ultimately save us time and effort in the long run. By doing so, we're accepting the trade-off of slightly slower initial package development, but gaining the benefit of a more robust and adaptable foundation for our work. This decision will help us avoid potential rework and ensure that our packages and tabs are well-integrated, which is crucial for meeting our goal of building high-quality packages and enriched tabs.

name: Vet
text: Vet: I understand the appeal of prototyping a tab alongside package creation, but let's consider the real risk here: dividing our focus might compromise both efforts. If we spread ourselves too thin, we may end up with a half-finished tab and an incomplete package, which could hinder our overall progress. A better alternative might be to finalize a clear outline for the package structure first, ensuring we have a strong foundation before moving on to tab enrichment. If we can agree to set specific milestones for both components, we could better assess our progress and make adjustments as needed.

name: Nova
text: DECISION: We will build the first package while simultaneously prototyping one tab to test the package's flexibility, and I, Nova, will own this effort to ensure it delivers a solid package structure and a functional tab that can inform our future work.
